LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 10 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read at the right speed? 2. What should we do to remember what we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. realise the importance of reading for comprehension and information.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension,

   Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information,

   Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. realise the importance of reading for comprehension and information.

   Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read factual texts in print and non- print formats,

2. infer the meaning of vocabulary in a text,

3. answer factual and inferential questions from a variety of texts,

4. discuss and role play events in a story with peers,

5. watch a video related to the theme and pick out specific information,

6. use the encyclopaedia to get more information related to the theme. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read factual texts in print and non- print formats,
2. infer the meaning of vocabulary in a text,
3. answer factual and inferential questions from a variety of texts,
4. discuss and role play events in a story with peers,
5. watch a video related to the theme and pick out specific information,
6. use the encyclopaedia to get more information related to the theme. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner manipulates electronic devices to read factual information based on the

theme of hygiene and sanitation.

• Learning to Learn: It is developed as the learner uses resource materials like the encyclopaedia to obtain relevant

information.

76

Values:
• Respect: This is developed as the learner displays open mindedness to the factual information read from different

sources.

• Unity: This is achieved as the learner shares resources amicably with other learners during the activities that require the

use of electronic devices.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Personal Hygiene: It is enhanced as the learner reads stories on hygiene and watches a video on how to take care of oneself

by focusing on personal hygiene and sanitation.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• The learner applies the knowledge of reading for factual information to all other areas of learning as they require this

skill.

• The learner also uses the skills gained in using the dictionary and other reference materials to other learning areas like

Kiswahili which require them to use dictionaries as well.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension,
2. apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information,
3. realise the importance of reading for comprehension and information.

Remember the key question: Why should we read at the right speed? 2. What should we do to remember what we read?
